Contract.title: Change commits construct and verify the Change trailer mechanically
Contract.Problem: Intervention I-009 records P-016: missing `Change:` trailers repeatedly caused review and history repair, then recurred on a closing commit while prose reminders failed to change behaviour. Attribution must be constructed and verified in the commit path, not remembered per free-form commit.
Contract.Change: A reusable repository commit routine constructs a commit for one explicit change id and explicit owned paths, appends the literal `Change: <id>` trailer, and reads back the created commit's parsed trailers and changed-path list. It refuses an empty selection, a path outside the supplied list, a missing or mismatched trailer, and any read-back failure; it never stages all dirty files, rewrites history or hides a failed verification. `grace5-execute` and `grace5-orchestrate` cite the routine for product, test, evidence, review and close-move commits; batch-only ledger commits follow their actual ownership rather than being assigned to a change. A failed verification stops the next handoff.

Constraints.Constraint: The routine is a repository tool, not a kernel command: no command, schema, record kind, receipt field, approval rule or closure rule changes.
Lifecycle semantics stay: final evidence remains kernel-counted on the actual candidate, and a red test-first commit remains allowed where the lifecycle allows it.
Path ownership is explicit; receipt revisions stay reachable, and no already referenced history is rewritten automatically.
L-01 is amended with the mechanical-attribution alternative, expected benefit, cost and removal criterion; no new kernel mechanism is recorded.
The routine uses git plumbing and porcelain only. A failed verification is reported and never suppressed, and a mismatched read-back is not repaired by amending a consumed commit.
An ordinary change: no version, pin, tag, migration boundary, migration row or release moves.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No kernel commit command and no new receipt or record field.
No automatic rewrite of already referenced history and no amendment of revisions consumed by receipts or later changes.
No staging of foreign dirty work, no adoption of unknown work, and no manufactured empty commit.
No replacement of a harness-native verified commit facility where it supports the required behaviour; the repository helper is the fallback.
No change to close, review or evidence semantics.

Acceptance.Criterion: Product, record and close-move commits created through the routine carry a parsed `Change: <id>` trailer and exactly the supplied paths.
An empty selection, a path outside the supplied list, a missing trailer or a mismatched read-back stops before the next change starts; foreign dirty work remains unstaged.
A red test-first commit remains allowed; a failed verification is reported and a hole in the read-back is not hidden.
Amending tip metadata does not silently rewrite revisions already consumed by receipts or later changes.
The execute and orchestrate skills cite the routine for every change-owned commit, and batch ledger commits are attributed by actual ownership.
The generated packages and CLI reference remain consistent with the changed skill text.
The new routine and its tests type-check with the rest of the kernel.

Decisions.Decision: The change id and owned paths are explicit arguments; implicit staging and inference from dirty state are refused.
The literal `Change: <id>` trailer is constructed once and read back from the created commit; a trailer mentioned only in prose does not count.
Batch-only ledger commits follow their actual ownership; they are not assigned to a change whose records they do not carry.
A failed read-back stops the next handoff; repair is a separate, owner-visible operation, never an automatic history rewrite.
A harness-native verified commit facility is used where it exists; the repository routine is the portable fallback.
A red test-first commit remains valid because the lifecycle, not the commit routine, decides when evidence is final.
